Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating behavioral transitions from semantic similarity. AAAI 2024’s [Spectral-Based GNN](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) models complementarity as combining relevance and dissimilarity, challenging similarity-only graph smoothing. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) predicts complementary products using a directed weighted graph projected from user–item interactions. [GLSRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.datak.2026.102606) propagates embeddings over a global directed item-transition graph, then combines global signals with local sequence modeling. These motivate asymmetric transition embeddings or a lightweight graph residual alongside SASRec; observed transitions alone do not establish complementarity.

Text-based results require attention to supervision and initialization. [ST2SI (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/) explicitly learns text-to-item-ID transition patterns but uses an LLM. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines BERT representations of titles, descriptions and reviews with SASRec, so its evidence does not directly establish effectiveness for a scratch-trained, title/description-only encoder. [MMSC (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3805712.3809684) targets substitute/complement inference but uses multimodal representations and LLM-assisted supervision, outside this benchmark’s resources.

A benchmark-compatible hypothesis: build sparse directed transition edges exclusively from training histories; separately encode titles/descriptions using randomly initialized token embeddings with mean pooling or a small CNN. Learn gated fusion with ID embeddings under next-item prediction, optionally adding a low-weight text–ID alignment objective. Treat semantic similarity and transition strength as separate measured signals, without assigning factual substitute/complement labels or asserting compatibility. Compare graph-only, text-only and combined variants using the prescribed macro validation HR@10; the searched literature does not establish that their combination will improve this setting.

---

Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from transient intent. [LSIDN (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) uses separate encoders and tailored denoising strategies for long- and short-term interests, emphasizing that both histories contain noise. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) learns latent intents through contrastive clustering, models recurring intent with Hawkes processes, and combines this with short-term attention. Intent labels are inferred rather than observed. [DSRec (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) separates historical aggregation from local intent, modulates short-term state evolution using interaction time gaps, and exchanges information through residual cross-fusion.

The closest routing match is [MARS (October 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07505): recurrent memory tracks with different half-lives preserve multiple temporal resolutions; sparse routing selects relevant resolutions. Its authors report that temporal diversity and selective routing each contribute beyond added capacity or hard windows, with larger advantages after behavioral shifts. For this SASRec task, a practical hypothesis is to retain the sequence encoder, add recent-history and slowly decaying historical pooling branches, then learn a gate using their representations, disagreement, and observed timestamp gaps. This is an implementation inference, not an established benchmark result. Repeated interactions can inform persistence without assuming repetition always means preference. Compare against single-stream SASRec and fixed fusion using macro validation HR@10; ablate timestamp inputs and routing separately. These approaches require no observed intent labels, reviews, demographics, or pretrained weights.

---

Recent evidence supports testing SASRec’s objective before adding architectural complexity. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) combines multiple negatives with calibrated gBCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence; its authors recommend 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75 as practical defaults. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax plus revised Transformer layers as a strong configuration, although that combined result does not isolate the loss contribution. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) approximates full CE by selecting informative high-scoring catalog subsets, reporting substantial memory savings while preserving recommendation quality. These findings motivate multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE comparisons; they do not establish an Electronics-specific improvement.

Hardness needs control: unobserved high-scoring items may be potential positives. [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies the pairwise objective to reduce false-negative influence during dynamic hard sampling; its evidence concerns implicit collaborative filtering, so transfer to SASRec requires validation. A [2024 sequential-recommendation sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity trade-offs, arguing against assuming hard or popularity sampling always wins. Practical experiment proposal: compare single-negative BCE, uniform multi-negative sampled softmax, and calibrated gBCE; then test a modest random/hard mixture. Exclude padding, the current positive, and known training-history positives from negative pools, without consulting held-out interactions. History masking prevents known-positive collisions but cannot identify latent false negatives. SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to interaction histories. Learned item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Final sequence features score candidates through shared item embeddings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
